zh: 他心里这样在想，她却说到就做，已转身走了出去，不知哪里找到了一只簇新的高脚木盆，提来一铫子的热水，冲到盆里；然后掀被来捉他的那双脚。『不要，不要！』胡雪岩往里一缩，『我这双脚从上海上船就没有洗过，太脏了。』『怕什么？』阿巧姐毫不迟疑地，『我路远迢迢赶了来，就是来服侍病人的；只要你好好复原，我比什么都高兴。』这两句话在胡雪岩听来，感激与感慨交并。兵荒马乱，九死一生；想到下落不明的亲人，快要饿死的杭州一城百姓，以及困在绝境，眼看着往地狱里一步一步在走的王有龄，常常会自问∶人生在世，到底为的什么；就为了受这种生不如死的苦楚？现在却不同了，人活在世界上，有苦也有乐；是苦是乐，全看自己的作为。真是『太上感应篇』上所说的∶『祸福无门，惟人自召』。这样转关念头，自己觉得一颗心如枯木逢春般，又管用了。脑筋亦已灵活；本来凡事都懒得去想，此刻却想得很多，想复很快。等阿巧姐替他将脚洗好，便又笑道∶『阿巧，送佛送到西天，索性替我再抹一抹身子。』『这不大妥当。你身子虚，受不得凉┅┅』
en: While he was thinking this, she had already gone to put her words into action. Somehow she found a brand-new wooden footbath on high legs. She brought a kettle of hot water, poured it into the basin, and lifted the quilt to take hold of his feet. “No, no!” Hu drew them back. “I have not washed them since I boarded the boat in Shanghai. They are filthy.” “What does that matter?” she said without hesitation. “I have come all this way to nurse a sick man. Nothing would make me happier than to see you recover properly.” Her words filled Hu with both gratitude and reflection. Through war and chaos, he had narrowly escaped death. Thinking of his missing family, the people of Hangzhou on the verge of starvation, and Wang Youling trapped in a hopeless position, moving step by step towards hell, he had often asked himself what people lived for. Was it merely to endure suffering worse than death? Now he felt differently. Life held joy as well as sorrow. Which one a person experienced depended on his own actions. It was just as the Treatise of the Exalted One on Response and Retribution said: misfortune and happiness have no fixed gate; people bring them upon themselves. With this change of thought, his heart seemed to come back to life, like a withered tree touched by spring. His mind grew active too. Where he had been too weary to think about anything, thoughts now came readily and quickly. Once A’qiao had washed his feet, he smiled. “A’qiao, since you have started a good deed, see it through. Give my body a wipe as well.” “That would not be wise. You are weak and must not catch cold…”

zh: 『不要紧！』胡雪岩将枯瘦的手臂伸出来，临空捣了两下，显得很有劲似地说∶『我自己觉得已经可以起床了。』『瞎说！你替我好好睡下去。』她将他的脚和手都塞入被中，硬扶他睡倒，而且还掖紧了棉被。『真的。阿巧，我已经好了。』『哪有这种事？这样一场病，哪里会说好就好？吃仙丹也没有这样灵法。』『人逢喜事精神爽，你就是仙丹。仙丹一到，百病全消。』『哼！』阿巧微微撇着嘴，『你就会灌米汤。睡吧！』她用纤行一指，将他的眼皮抹上。等她转身，他的眼又睁开了。望着帐顶想心事；要想知道的事很多，而眼前却只有阿巧好谈。
en: “It does not matter!” Hu thrust out his withered arm and punched the air twice, trying to look vigorous. “I feel well enough to get up.” “Nonsense! Lie down properly.” She tucked his feet and hands beneath the quilt, pressed him back onto the bed, and pulled the covering snugly around him. “Truly, A’qiao, I am well again.” “How can you be? After an illness like this, you do not recover just because you say so. Even an elixir could not work that fast.” “Good fortune lifts the spirits. You are my elixir. Once it arrives, every illness vanishes.” “Hmph!” Her lips curled slightly. “You are good at sweet talk. Go to sleep.” With a slender finger she brushed his eyelids shut. As soon as she turned away, his eyes opened again. He stared at the canopy and thought. There were many things he wanted to know, but for the moment, A’qiao was the one person he wished to talk to.

zh: 阿巧却好久不来；他忍不住喊出声来，而答应的却是萧家骥，『胡先生，』他说，『你不宜过于劳神。此刻半夜两点钟了，请安置吧！』『阿巧呢？』胡雪岩问道∶『她睡在哪里？』做批发生意的大商号，备有客房客铺，无足为奇，但从不招待堂客；有些商家的客户，甚至忌讳堂客，因为据说月事中的妇女会冲犯所供的财神。杨坊的这家招牌也叫『大记』，专营海鲜杂货批发的商号，虽然比较开通，不忌妇女出入，但单间的客房不多；所以阿巧姐是由萧家骥代为安排，借住在大记的一个伙计家中，与此人的新婚妻子同榻睡了一夜。『今天不行了，是轮到那伙计回家睡的日子；十天才有这么一天，阿巧姐说∶』人家喷喷香、簇簇新的新娘子；怎好耽误他们夫妻的恩爱？「那伙计倒很会做人，一再说不要紧；是阿巧姐自己不肯。『』那末今天睡在哪里呢？『『喏，』萧家骥指着置在一旁的一扇门板，两张条凳说∶『我已经预备好了，替她搭「起倒铺」。不过——。』他笑笑没有再说下去。神情诡秘，令人起疑，胡雪岩当然要追问∶『不过什么？』『我看这张床蛮大，不如让阿巧姐就睡在胡先生脚后头。』萧家骥又说，『她要这里搭铺就为了服侍方便；睡在一床上，不更加方便了吗？』不知他是正经话，还是戏谑？也不知阿巧姐本人的意思究竟如何？胡雪岩只有微笑不答。
en: She did not return for a long time. Unable to restrain himself, he called out. It was Xiao who answered. “Mr Hu, you must not tire yourself. It is two in the morning. Please rest.” “Where is A’qiao? Where is she sleeping?” Large wholesale firms commonly provided guest rooms and beds, but they did not ordinarily accommodate women. Some merchants and their customers even objected to a woman’s presence, believing that a menstruating woman might offend the God of Wealth worshipped on the premises. Yang’s Ningbo firm, also called Daji, specialized in wholesaling seafood and sundries. It was comparatively broad-minded and did not forbid women to come and go, but it had few private guest rooms. Xiao had therefore arranged for A’qiao to stay at a clerk’s house, where she had shared a bed with the man’s newly married wife for one night. “That will not do tonight. It is the clerk’s turn to sleep at home, and he gets only one night in ten. Sister A’qiao said, ‘Such a fresh, sweet young bride! How could I keep the two of them apart?’ The clerk was very considerate and insisted it did not matter, but she would not agree.” “Then where will she sleep tonight?” “There.” Xiao pointed to a door panel and two benches standing to one side. “I have everything ready to make her a temporary bed. Still—” He smiled and said no more. Something knowing in his expression invited suspicion, and Hu naturally pressed him. “Still what?” “This bed looks quite large. Why not let her sleep at the foot of it? She wants to stay in this room so that she can look after you. Would sharing the bed not be more convenient still?” Hu could not tell whether he was serious or joking, nor did he know what A’qiao herself intended. He could only smile without answering.

zh: 到最后，萧家骥还是替阿巧姐搭了『起倒铺』；被褥衾枕自然是她自己铺设。等侍候病人服了药，关好房门，胡雪岩开口了。『你的褥子太薄，又没有帐子，不知睡到我里床来！』他拍拍身边。正在卸妆的阿巧姐没有说话，抱衾相就；不过为了行动方便，睡的是外床——宁波人讲究床铺；那张黄杨木雕花的床极大，两个人睡还绰绰有余。里床搁板上置一盏洋灯，——捻得小小的一点光照着她那个葱绿缎子的紧身小夹袄；看在胡雪岩眼里，又起了相逢在梦中的感觉。『阿巧！你该讲讲你的事了吧？』『说来话长。』阿巧很温柔地说∶『你这半夜也累了；刚吃过药好好睡一觉。明天再谈。』『我现在精神很好。』『精神好自然好。你听，』阿巧姐说，『鸡都在叫了。后半夜这一觉最要紧，睡吧！好在我人都来了，你还有什么好急的？』这句话的意思很深，足够胡雪岩想好半天。到底病势初转，精神不够，很快地便觉得困倦，一觉睡到天亮。
en: In the end, Xiao did set up a temporary bed for her. Naturally, she arranged her own mattress, quilt, and pillow. Once she had given the patient his medicine and closed the door, Hu spoke. “Your mattress is too thin, and you have no bed curtains. You would do better to sleep on the inner side here.” He patted the place beside him. A’qiao, who was removing her hair ornaments and make-up, said nothing. She brought her quilt over, but took the outer side so that she could get up easily. Ningbo people took pride in their beds. This one, carved from boxwood, was enormous, with more than enough room for two. An oil lamp stood on a shelf at the inner side, its flame turned low. Its faint light fell on her close-fitting, light lined jacket of pale green satin. Looking at her, Hu once again felt that their reunion was a dream. “A’qiao, surely it is time you told me what has happened to you?” “It is a long story,” she replied gently. “You have tired yourself tonight and have just taken your medicine. Sleep well. We can talk tomorrow.” “I feel very alert now.” “It is good that you do. But listen—the cocks are already crowing. These last hours of sleep before dawn matter most. Go to sleep. I am here now. What is there to hurry about?” There was a depth of meaning in this that gave Hu plenty to think about. But his illness had only just begun to recede, and his strength was limited. Soon he grew drowsy and slept until daylight.

zh: 他醒她也醒了，急急要起床料理，胡雪岩却愿她多睡一会；拖住她说∶『天太冷，不要起来。我们好好谈谈。』『谈什么？』阿巧姐说，『但愿你早早复原；回到上海再说。』『我昨天晚上想过了，只要这一次能平平安过去，我再也不做官了；安安分分做生意，能够跟几个好朋友常在一起叙叙，我就心满意足了。』『你只晓得朋友！』阿巧姐是微带怨态的神情，『就不替自己打算打算。』替他自己打算，当然也就要包括她在内。言外之意，相当微妙；胡雪岩很沉着地不作表示，只是问说∶『你是怎么从何家出来的？现在可以告诉我了吧！』『当然要告诉你的。不过你处处为朋友，听了只怕心里会难过。』她的意思是将何桂清当作胡雪岩的朋友——这个朋友现在惨不可言。只为在常州一念之差，落得个『革职拿问』的处分；迁延两年，多靠薛焕替他支吾敷衍，然而『逃犯』的况味也受够了。
en: When he woke, she woke too and hurried to get up and attend to him. Hu wanted her to rest a little longer. Holding her back, he said, “It is too cold. Do not get up yet. Let us have a proper talk.” “About what? I only want you to get well soon. Everything else can wait until we are back in Shanghai.” “I thought it over last night. If I come safely through this, I shall never be an official again. I shall mind my own business and be content if I can meet a few good friends regularly for a chat.” “You think only of your friends,” she said with a trace of reproach. “You never make plans for yourself.” Plans for himself would naturally have to include her. The implication was delicate. Hu showed no reaction, but calmly asked, “How did you leave the He household? Can you tell me now?” “Of course I must tell you. But you are always thinking of your friends. I am afraid it will distress you.” She was counting He Guiqing among Hu’s friends—and his situation was now pitiable indeed. One mistaken decision at Changzhou had brought dismissal and an order for his arrest and investigation. For two years the matter had dragged on, largely because Xue Huan had contrived excuses and delays on his behalf. Yet he had suffered more than enough of a fugitive’s existence.

zh: 『这种日子不是人过的。』阿巧姐喟叹着说∶『人嘛是个黑人，哪里都不能去；听说有客人来拜，先要打听清楚，来做什么？最怕上海县的县大老爷来拜；防是来捉人的。「白天不做亏心事，半夜敲门心不惊」这句俗语，我算是领教过了，真正一点不错。我都这样子，你想想本人心里的味道？』『叫我，就狠一狠心，自己去投案。』『他也常这样说；不过说说而已，就是狠不下心来。现在——。』现在，连这种提心吊胆的日子也快不多了。从先帝驾崩，幼主嗣位，两宫太后垂帘听政，垂用恭王，朝中又是一番气象；为了激励士气，凡是丧师辱国的文武官员，都要严办。最不利的是，曾国藩调任两江都督，朝命统辖江苏、安徽、江西、浙江四省军务；四省官员，文到巡抚，武到提督，悉归节制。何桂清曾经托人关说，希望能给他一个效力赎罪的机会，而得到的答复只有四个字∶『爱莫能助。』『半个月以前，有人来说，曾大人保了个姓李的道台，领兵来守上海。这位李道台，据说一到上海就要接薛抚台的手；他是曾大人的门生，自然听老师的话。薛抚台再想帮忙也帮不上了。为此之故——。』为此，何桂清不能不作一个最后的打算∶家事已作了处分，姬妆亦都遣散，阿巧姐就是这样下堂的。
en: “It was no life for a human being,” A’qiao sighed. “With his status so compromised, he could go nowhere. Whenever a visitor was announced, we first had to find out exactly why he had come. Most frightening of all was a call from the Shanghai magistrate: we feared he might have come to make an arrest. I have learned the truth of that saying, ‘Do no wrong by day, and a midnight knock will not frighten you.’ It could not be truer. If I felt like that, imagine how he felt himself.” “In his place, I should have steeled myself and surrendered.” “He often said the same. But saying it was all he could do; he could never bring himself to act. Now…” Now even those days of constant apprehension were nearly over. Since the late emperor’s death, the accession of a child sovereign, and the two empress dowagers’ assumption of government behind the curtain with Prince Gong in high favour, a new spirit prevailed at court. To restore morale, civil and military officials who had lost armies and dishonoured the state were to be dealt with severely. Worst of all, Zeng Guofan had been appointed governor-general of Liangjiang and placed in command of military affairs in Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, and Zhejiang. All officials in those four provinces, up to governors in the civil administration and commanders-in-chief in the military, were subject to his authority. He Guiqing had sent intermediaries to ask for an opportunity to redeem himself through service. The reply had been brief: willing to help, but unable to do so. “Half a month ago someone brought word that Mr Zeng had recommended an intendant named Li to lead troops to defend Shanghai. They say that as soon as he arrives he will take over from Governor Xue. He is Mr Zeng’s pupil and will naturally obey his teacher. Governor Xue will no longer be able to help, however much he wishes. Because of that—” Because of that, He had to make his final arrangements. He settled his household affairs and dismissed his concubines. That was how A’qiao had left his household.

zh: 想想他待她不错，在这个时候，分袂而去，未免问心不安。无奈何桂清执意不回；她也就只好听从了。『那天，他也总要为你的后半辈子打算打算。』胡雪岩说∶『不过，他剩下几个钱，这两年坐吃山空，恐怕所余已经无几。』『过日子倒用不了多少，都给人骗走了，这个说，可以替他到京走门路；那个说某某人那里送笔礼。这种塞狗洞的钱，也不知道花了多少。』阿巧姐说，『临走以前，他跟我说，要凑两千银子给我。我一定不要。』『你倒也够义气。不过，这种乱世，说老实话∶求人不如求己。』『我也不是毫无打算的，我有一只小箱子托七姑奶奶替我收着；那里面一点东西，总值三、五万。到了上海我交给你。』『交给我做什么？』胡雪岩问道∶『我现在还没心思来替你经营。』阿巧姐先不作声，一面眨眼，一面咬指甲，仿佛有极要紧的事在思索似的。胡雪岩是从钱塘江遥别王有龄的那一刻，便有万念俱灰之感，什么事都不愿、也不能想，因此恹恹成病，如今病势虽已脱险，而且好得很快，但懒散如旧，所以不愿去猜她的心事，只侧着脸象面对着他所喜爱的古玉似的，恣意鉴赏。
en: Remembering how well he had treated her, she had felt uneasy about leaving him at such a moment. But he would not change his mind, and she had no choice but to obey. “He must have tried to provide for the rest of your life before you left,” Hu said. “Though how much could he have had left? Two years of living on his capital must have brought him close to the end.” “Ordinary expenses did not amount to much. Most of it was swindled out of him. One man said he could work through influential contacts in the capital; another said a gift must be sent to someone or other. Who knows how much money went down those holes? Before I left, he said he would scrape together two thousand taels for me. I would not take it.” “That was loyal of you. But in times like these, to be frank, you are better off relying on yourself than on others.” “I have not left myself entirely without provision. I entrusted a little chest to the Seventh Lady. The things in it must be worth thirty to fifty thousand taels. When we return to Shanghai, I shall give it to you.” “What for? I have no heart for managing investments for you just now.” A’qiao said nothing. She blinked and bit a fingernail, as though considering something of great importance. Ever since Hu had bade his distant farewell to Wang across the Qiantang River, he had felt that every desire was extinguished. He had neither wished nor been able to think about anything, and had sunk into illness. Though he was now out of danger and recovering quickly, the old listlessness remained. He did not care to guess her thoughts. Turning his face towards her, he merely admired her at leisure, as he might contemplate a piece of ancient jade he loved.

zh: 算一算有六年没有这样看过她了。离乱六年，是一段漫长的岁月，多少人生死茫茫，音信杳然，多少人升沉浮降，荣枯异昔，而想到六年前的阿巧姐，只如隔了一夜做了个梦；当时形容清晰地浮现在脑际，两相比较，有变了的，也有不变的。变得最明显的是全体态，此刻丰腴了些；当时本嫌纤瘦，所以这一变是变得更美了；也更深沉老练了。不变的是她这双眼中的情竟，依然那么深，那么纯；似乎她心目中除了一个胡雪岩以外，连她自己都不关心。转念到此，他那颗心就象冷灰发现一粒火星；这是火种复炽的开始，他自己都觉得珍贵得很。
en: It had been six years since he had looked at her in this way. Six years of war and separation was a long time. How many people had vanished, their survival uncertain, their whereabouts unknown? How many had risen or fallen, their fortunes utterly changed? Yet A’qiao as she had been six years ago seemed only a night and a dream away. Her appearance then came vividly before his mind. Comparing the two, he saw what had changed and what had not. The most obvious change was in her figure: she was fuller now. Before, she had been rather too slender, so the change had made her more beautiful. She was also more composed and worldly-wise. What had not changed was the feeling in her eyes, as deep and pure as ever. It seemed that, in her mind, there was no one but Hu Xueyan—not even herself. At that thought, a spark appeared among the cold ashes of his heart. It was the beginning of a rekindled fire, and he himself felt how precious it was.

zh: 于是他不自觉地伸手去握住她的手；感慨地说∶『这趟我真是九死一生——不是怕路上有什么危险，胆子小；是我的心境。从杭州到宁波，一路上我的心冷透了；整天躺在床上在想，一个人为啥要跟另外一个人有感情？如果没有感情，他是他，我是我，用不着替他牵肠挂肚，所以我自己对自己说，将来等我心境平静了，对什么人都要冷淡些。』一口气说到这里，有些气喘，停了下来；阿巧姐不曾听出他的语气未完，只当他借题发挥，顿时脸色大变。『你这些话，』她问，『是不是特为说给我听的？』『是的——。』说了这两个字，胡雪岩才发觉她的神情有异；立刻明白她是误会了，赶紧又接了一句∶『这话我什么人面前都没说过；只跟你一人说，是有道理的。不晓得你猜得着，猜不着？』意思仍然令人莫名其妙，但他急于解释误会的态度，她是看出来的，心先放了一半，另一半要听他下一句话如何？『你不要让我猜了！你晓得的，赌心思，跟别人我还可以较量较量；在你面前差了一大截。』胡雪岩笑了，笑容并不好年；人瘦显得口大，两颗虎牙看上去象獠牙。但毕竟是高兴的笑容，阿巧姐还是乐意看到的。
en: Without quite realizing it, he reached for her hand. “I came close to death on this journey,” he said with feeling. “I do not mean that I was timid or feared the dangers on the road. I mean what happened to my heart. From Hangzhou to Ningbo, it grew utterly cold. I lay in bed all day asking why one person should care for another. Without affection, he could be himself and I could be myself, and I need never fret over him. So I told myself that, once my mind was at peace again, I would be more distant towards everyone.” He had said this in a single rush and had to pause for breath. A’qiao did not realize that he had more to say. Taking it as an indirect message to her, she changed colour. “Are you saying this especially for me?” “Yes—” Only then did Hu notice her expression. He understood her mistake at once and hastened to add, “I have never said this to anyone else. There is a reason why I am telling you alone. I wonder whether you can guess it.” The meaning remained obscure, but she could see how anxious he was to correct the misunderstanding. Half reassured, she waited for what he would say next. “Do not make me guess. You know I can match wits with other people, but I am far behind you.” Hu smiled. It was not a handsome smile. His wasted face made his mouth seem large, and the two pointed canine teeth looked almost like fangs. But it was a happy smile, and she was glad to see it.

zh: 『你还是那样会说话。』他正一正脸色说∶『我特为谈我的心境，是想告诉你的一句话；此刻我的想法变过了。』『怎么变法？』『人还是要有感情的。就为它受罪，为它死——。』一句话未完，一只又软又暖的手掩在他口上∶『什么话不好说；说这些没轻重的话！』『好，不说，不说。你懂我的意思就可以了。』胡雪岩问道∶『你刚才好象在想心事？何妨跟我谈谈。』『要谈的话很多。现在这样子，你没心思听，我也没心思说，一切都不必急，等你病养好了再说。』『我的病一时养不好的。好在是——。』他想说『好在是死不了的』；只为她忌讳说『死』，所以猛然咽住；停了一下又说∶『一两天我就想回上海。』『那怎么行？』『没有什么不行。在宁波，消息不灵，又没有事好做；好人都要闷出病来，怎么会养得好病？』
en: “You still know just what to say.” He grew serious. “I spoke of my state of mind because there was one thing I wanted to tell you: I have changed my mind now.” “How?” “People must have feelings after all. Even if they suffer for them, even if they die for them—” Before he finished, a warm, soft hand covered his mouth. “With so many things you could say, why talk so recklessly?” “Very well, I shall not say it. So long as you understand.” He asked, “You seemed to be thinking hard about something just now. Why not tell me?” “There is much to say. But as things are, you have no heart to listen, and I have no heart to speak. Nothing need be hurried. We can talk once you are well.” “I shall not be fully well for some time. Fortunately—” He had meant to say that at least he would not die, but remembering her objection to the word, he stopped himself. After a pause he continued, “In a day or two, I mean to return to Shanghai.” “How can you?” “Why not? Here in Ningbo, news is slow and there is nothing to do. A healthy man would fall ill from sheer boredom. How can a sick one recover?”

zh: 『那是没有办法的事。你刚刚才有点好，数九寒天冒海风上路，万一病势反复；在汪洋大海里，叫天天不应，叫地地不灵，那就是两条人命。』『怎么呢？』『你不想想，万一你有个三长两短，我除了跳海，还有什么路好走？』是这样生死相共的情分，胡雪岩再也不忍拂她的意了。但是，他自己想想，只要饮食当心，加上阿巧姐细心照料，实在无大关碍。不过，若非医生同意，不但不能塞阿巧姐的嘴，只怕萧家骥也未见得答应。因此，他决定嘱咐萧家骥私下向医生探问。但始终找不到机会；因为阿巧姐自起床以后，几乎就不曾离开过他——天又下雪了，萧家骥劝她就在屋子里『做市』；就着一只熊熊然的炭盆，煎药煮粥做菜，都在那间屋里。胡雪岩倒觉得热闹有趣，用杭州的谚语笑她是『螺蛳壳里做道场』；但也因此，虽萧家骥就在眼前，却无从说两句私话。
en: “It cannot be helped. You have only just begun to improve. If you travel in the bitterest winter cold, exposed to the sea wind, and your illness returns, there will be no one to help in the middle of the ocean, however loudly we call. It would mean two lives lost.” “Why two?” “Have you not thought? If anything happened to you, what could I do but throw myself into the sea?” Faced with such devotion, extending to life and death, Hu could no longer bear to oppose her. Privately, however, he thought that with care over his diet and A’qiao’s attentive nursing, there would be no great risk. Yet without the doctor’s agreement, he could not silence her objections, and Xiao would probably object as well. He decided to ask Xiao to sound out the doctor privately. But he could never find an opportunity. From the moment she got up, A’qiao scarcely left his side. Snow had begun to fall again, and Xiao suggested that she set up all her operations in the room. With a brazier burning brightly, she prepared medicine, cooked gruel, and made dishes there. Hu found the bustle lively and amusing. Using a Hangzhou saying, he teased her about conducting a grand religious ceremony inside a snail shell. But it meant that, although Xiao was right before him, there was no chance for a private word.

zh: 不过，也不算白耗功夫。萧家骥一面帮阿巧姐做『下手』，帮她料理饭食，一面将这几天的情形都告诉了胡雪岩。据说黄呈忠、范汝增跟英国领事夏福礼的谈判很顺利，答应尽力保护外侨；有两名长毛侵袭英国教士，已经抓来『正法』。而且还布告安民，准老百姓在四门以外做生意；宁波的市面，大致已经恢复了。『得力的是我们的那批米。民以食为天，粮食不起恐慌，人心就容易安定。』萧家骥劝慰似地说∶『胡先生，你也可以稍稍弥补遗憾了。』『这是阴功积德的好事。』阿巧姐接口说道∶『就看这件好事，老太太就一定会有菩萨保佑，逢凶化吉，遇难成祥。』胡雪岩不作声。一则以喜，一则以悲；没有什么适当的话好表达他的复杂的心情。
en: The time was not wholly wasted. Helping A’qiao prepare the food, Xiao told Hu everything that had happened over the past few days. Apparently the negotiations between Huang Chengzhong and Fan Ruzeng and the British consul, Xiafuli, had gone well. The commanders had promised to do all they could to protect foreign residents. Two rebel soldiers who had attacked a British missionary had been arrested and executed. Proclamations had also been issued to reassure the population, allowing trade outside the four gates. Business in Ningbo had largely returned to normal. “Our rice made the difference. Food is the people’s first necessity. Once there is no panic over grain, it is easier for them to settle down,” Xiao said consolingly. “At least that should ease some of your regret, Mr Hu.” “It is a good deed that earns unseen merit,” A’qiao added. “For that deed alone, the Bodhisattva will surely protect your mother, turn danger into safety, and bring her through her troubles.” Hu remained silent. Joy and sorrow mingled in him, and he could find no words adequate to express what he felt.

zh: 『有句要紧话要告诉胡先生，那笔米价，大记的人问我怎么算法？是卖了拆帐、还是作价给他们？我说米先领了去，怎样算法，要问了你才能定规；如果他们不肯答应，我作不了主，米只好原船运回。大记答应照我的办法；现在要问胡先生了。照我看，拆算比较合算！』『不！』胡雪岩断然答道∶『我不要钱。』那末要什么呢？胡雪岩要的是米；要的是运粮的船，只等杭州一旦克复，三天以内就要。他的用意是很容易明白；等杭州从长毛手里夺了回来，必定饿殍载途，灾民满城，那时所需要的就是米。『何必这么做？』萧家骥劝他∶『胡先生，在商言商，你的算盘是大家佩服的，这样做法，不等于将本钱「搁煞」在那里。而况杭州克复，遥遥无期。』『不见得。气运要转的。』胡雪岩显得有些激动，『长毛搞的这一套，翻覆无常，我看他们不会久了。三、五年的功夫，就要完蛋。』『三、五年是多少辰光，利上盘利，一担米变成两三担米；你就为杭州百姓，也该盘算盘算。』『话不错！』胡雪岩又比较平静了，『我有我的想法，第一、我始终没有绝望，也许援兵会到，杭州城可以不破，如果粮道可以打通，我立刻就要运米去接济，那时候万一不凑手，岂不误了大事；第二、倘或杭州真的失守，留着米在那里，等克复以后，随时可以启运——这是一种自己安慰自己的希望；说穿了，是自己骗自己，总算我对杭州也尽到心了。』『这也有道理，我就跟大记去交涉。』
en: “There is something important I must ask you,” Xiao continued. “The people at Daji wanted to know how the rice was to be accounted for. Should they sell it and divide the proceeds with us, or take it over at an agreed price? I told them to receive the rice first. The terms could only be settled after I had asked you. If they would not agree to that, I had no authority to do otherwise, and the rice would have to return on the same boats. Daji accepted. Now I must ask you. In my view, sharing the proceeds would be the more advantageous arrangement.” “No,” Hu answered firmly. “I do not want money.” What did he want, then? Rice—and vessels to carry it. Once Hangzhou was recaptured, he wanted them available within three days. His purpose was easily understood. When the city was recovered from the rebels, the roads would surely be strewn with those who had starved, and the city full of distressed survivors. What they would need was rice. “Why arrange it like that?” Xiao urged. “Speaking strictly as a businessman—and everyone admires your calculations—would this not leave your capital tied up and idle? Besides, the recapture of Hangzhou may be a long way off.” “Not necessarily. Fortunes will turn,” Hu said with some agitation. “The rebels’ conduct is erratic and unreliable. I do not think they can last. In three or five years they will be finished.” “Three or five years is a long time. With interest compounding, one dan of rice can become two or three. Even for the sake of Hangzhou’s people, you ought to consider the calculation.” “That is true.” Hu grew calmer again. “But I have my own reasons. First, I have not entirely given up hope. Reinforcements may arrive, and Hangzhou may not fall. If the supply route can be opened, I shall want to send rice at once. If it were not readily available, we might lose the opportunity. Second, if the city does fall, keeping rice ready means it can be dispatched whenever the place is recovered. It is a hope with which I comfort myself. To put it plainly, I am deceiving myself, but at least I shall have done what I can for Hangzhou.” “That makes sense too. I shall negotiate with Daji on those terms.”
